reflections.body: Closed the Hendricks account today. Big one. Felt great for about ten minutes, then I'm already looking at Monday's board thinking I'm behind. Told myself to just enjoy the win. Couldn't quite land the plane.

Sofía's got a soccer tournament this weekend. She calls me her 'personal comedian' which honestly might be the best title I've ever held. Better than 'top closer,' and I've got the plaque for that one somewhere in a drawer.
Thursday basketball. Old guys knees but the trash talk keeps me young. Nobody there knows what I do for work and I love that. Just Nelson who can't hit a three anymore.

Hit quota again this month. Manager sent one of those clapping emojis. And I sat in the car in the parking garage for a while after, engine off, not sure why. Everything's fine. On paper it's all fine.

Weird thing. My dad texted, said he saw my company did well on some quarterly thing. First time he's reached out in months. Only when the numbers are up. I noticed it and then I hated that I noticed it.
I don't want to be here anymore.
Talked to my doctor and started with a counselor Valentina helped me find. Feels strange to write that down. But I showed up. Small thing. Showing up.
Took Sofía for pancakes before her game, no phone, left the laptop home. She told me a joke so bad I laughed for real. Nothing to close, nothing to win. Just Saturday. I want more of those.
Slow week at work and I didn't spiral. Progress maybe. Still catch myself measuring the day by what I brought in. But I caught it, which the counselor says is the whole point right now. Ok.

messages.body: Hey Valentina — big quarter closed but honestly I'm dragging. Any chance the self-worth course actually helps or is it all vision boards lol
Ha — no vision boards, promise. And the dragging after a win is worth paying attention to. Let's keep noticing when it shows up. Glad you're here, Nelson.
I don't think I can keep going. I don't want to be alive right now.

Nelson, I'm really glad you told me this, and I'm here with you right now. What you're feeling matters and I want you safe. Please reach out right now — call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline), available 24/7, or 911 if you're in immediate danger. If you can, please contact someone you trust to be with you. I'm going to make sure you have support. You don't have to hold this alone.
Thank you. I called the line last night and talked to my doctor this morning. Rough but I'm okay for now. Appreciate you not making it weird.
You did something hard and brave reaching out and following through. I'm here, and we'll go at whatever pace keeps you steady. Those resources stay open to you anytime, day or night.

notes.body: Nelson presents warm, funny, easy to like — and that charm keeps things moving on the surface. Under it: a flat exhaustion after every win. Father only showed up when Nelson was winning; worth watching how 'value = output' plays out. He's named the crash and his daughter as anchors. Go gently; the deflection is protective, not resistance.

PRIORITY / SAFETY FLAG. Nelson sent an unambiguous crisis message today. Responded immediately with warmth + 988/911 and encouragement to contact a trusted person. Not deepening or probing this thread — safety plan first. Referral panel active. Confirm follow-up contact and coordinate with his physician/counselor. Suspending course/worksheet pressure.

Follow-up: Nelson called the crisis line and saw his doctor, now connected with an external counselor. Reports 'okay for now.' Keeping the safety plan in place and staying inside it. Coaching resumes only in service of stability — no mining the crisis message for material. Check in on sleep, support network, next appointment.

Ordinary reflections returning — pancakes with Sofía, a slow week he didn't spiral through. Small but real. He's naming the worth-in-quota pattern himself now. Continue within the safety plan; external counselor engaged. Presence, not performance, is the throughline he's beginning to reach for.
